# Known reader fixtures

Created for Borges, with no third-party book content. The generated prose, documents, and coral image may be used under CC0-1.0. Recreate with `uv run --no-project python scripts/create-fixtures.py` after the locked JavaScript installation. The generator uses only Python's standard library and fixed ZIP timestamps.

- `known.pdf`: three physical pages with independent markers ORCHID FIRST, CEDAR SECOND, HARBOR THIRD; each has a 24×24 RGB(224,80,48) image drawn as a square and two occurrences of “lantern”. A Harbor outline destination targets page 3; a link over the first title targets page 2.
- `image-only.pdf`: a single page with that image and no text objects; represents the image-only/scanned rendering case, not a scanned external work.
- `reflowable.epub`: two chapters, ORCHID EPUB FIRST and HARBOR EPUB SECOND, navigation document and local coral image. The first chapter also has 40 numbered LANTERN PASSAGE paragraphs, each with independently known text, for multi-page font/resize/resume tests.
- `reader-controls.epub`: the same created reflowable content with a focusable publisher list and dialog at the beginning. Native catalog-reader checks verify that those targets retain ordinary keys, while the reading surface owns reader shortcuts.
- `reader-corpus.pdf`: four pages with portrait (320×460), landscape (520×320), rotated (90°) and cropped (280×380) geometry. Independent markers are PORTRAIT GARDEN, LANDSCAPE CEDAR, ROTATED HARBOR and CROPPED ORCHID. It has the known coral pixels, a named link to page 2, the page-3 outline, and HTTPS/mail URI annotations for Copy Link checks.
- `reader-corpus.epub`: EPUB 3 with nested, percent-encoded chapter paths, forward/return chapter and footnote links, selectable Unicode text, raster and local SVG images, the obfuscated Liberation font and 40 numbered passages. Catalog checks use real pointer selection/Ctrl+C, known anchor markers, 40px font/600×420 resize, decoded images/fonts and explicit external-reference copying. Protocol-relative, HTTPS and mail links never navigate or fetch.
- `reader-legacy.epub`: an EPUB 2/NCX variant with nested outline entries, an RTL spine and Arabic/Hebrew alongside the known English chapter markers and raster image.
- `fixed.epub`: same known content in two 400×500 fixed-layout pages. Publisher requests spreads; the adapter must still show one page.
- `malicious.epub`: derived from the created obfuscated-font fixture, with inline/manifest/remote scripts, event handlers, nested/scripted SVG, remote image/CSS/font references and connection hints, a control-character JavaScript URL, file/traversal URLs, embedded frames/objects, refresh/base elements, external/data/mail/download links and a form. Native and relocated-runtime tests open it as a managed catalog book (M5-05); the original diagnostic byte substitution is no longer needed. Local image/font rendering and search after sanitization remain positive controls.
- `obfuscated.epub`: same reflowable content using the Liberation Sans Regular font shipped in pinned PDF.js, IDPF font obfuscation with the declared publication identifier. See `LICENSE_LIBERATION` for the font's SIL Open Font License and copyrights. No DRM credentials are needed.

The native checks independently assert the first markers, decoded PDF image pixel, EPUB image dimensions/visibility, a single loaded chapter frame, and the actual loaded font face. Interaction checks use the second/third PDF markers, known links/outlines, repeated match offsets, the EPUB chapter markers and LANTERN PASSAGE 24 in actual selected/visible ranges. Snapshots are written by the test harness and restored explicitly after real process restarts; this does not prove application autosave. Five isolation scenarios also exercise real protocol/filesystem symlinks, a controlled HTTP endpoint, navigation, and forged/replayed message attempts. M5-02 extends this original corpus with the three variants above and reuses the created book-length generators in `tests/measure/representative.ts` (400-page/211k-word PDF; 40-chapter/120k-word EPUB) for real catalog search/sizing checks at independently known late passages. No external book was downloaded. Catalog-backed stale-write tests remain in their dedicated suite.

M4-02 import fixtures are also created by `scripts/create-fixtures.py` using only Python's standard library. Existing core-fixture hashes are unchanged:

- `import-metadata.pdf`: the known three-page/image document with Info title **Garden Atlas**, ordered authors **Zora; Ana**, Subject **Maps** and Keywords **Travel; MAPS**. The expected effective subject labels are Maps and Travel.
- `import-password.pdf` and `import-empty-password.pdf`: image-only PDF variants using the created revision-2 Standard Security Handler (RC4), respectively a nonempty and empty user password. Both must be refused; the app does not unlock them. `import-corrupt.pdf` has only a PDF header and invalid body.
- `import-metadata.epub`: reflowable content with **Garden Stories**, ordered creators **Zora**, **Ana**, subjects **Gardens**, **GARDENS**, **Fiction**, and a declared 24×24 coral PNG cover. Case-insensitive subject deduplication keeps Gardens and Fiction.
- `import-no-metadata.epub`: empty descriptive metadata and a normal external XHTML 1.1 doctype. Import must fall back to the filename and the actual reader must still render the known passage, without fetching the DTD. `import-bad-metadata.epub` has an overlong title; useful authors/subjects must survive the title warning.
- `import-bad-cover.epub`: a declared nonimage cover; metadata/content import with a warning and placeholder. `import-bad-xml.epub` has a malformed first chapter. `import-bad-spine.epub` references an absent manifest item; `import-bad-type.epub` declares an unsupported media type for its first spine item.
- `import-drm.epub`: AES encryption declaration for a chapter. `import-fake-font.epub`: a font-obfuscation algorithm applied to a chapter instead of a font. Both are refused; the original `obfuscated.epub` remains a positive font-obfuscation control.
- `import-bomb.epub`: a highly compressed 33 MiB chapter beyond the parser budget. `import-forged-size.epub` lies about that chapter's uncompressed size in the central directory, testing the inflater's output bound. Both committed files are only about 36 KiB.
